(u2, else) -> u2

(u0, has_door_key & !door_open, u1) -> 0.1

(u2, !door_open & has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
feedback: The transition/reward core is largely sound: guards are predicate-only over has_door_key and door_open, every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant or persistent configurations, the recurring cycle (key lands -> answer -> relock -> next key) is fully covered, regressions out of u2 are explicit (u2->u0 and u2->u1), rewards are dense but bounded (0.1 on a key landing, 1.0 per answer) with no farmable self-loops, and the paper format including a nonempty FINAL_STATES header is respected. Two problems block acceptance. (1) FINAL_STATES is not accepting for this task. The task requires every gift in the episode (typically 3-13) to be answered, so acceptance cannot be earned by the first answer. u2 is entered at the very first answer while u0 is not final, so the final set {u2} only recognizes success if the episode happens to end while the door is still open - the reference trace ends with the door shut and the machine in u0, which would be scored a failure despite 8/8 gifts answered. Conversely, if reaching a final state signals task completion, the first answer terminates the task and later gifts earn nothing, contradicting the machine's own u2->u1/u2->u0 regressions. The accepting states are the obligation-free states: FINAL_STATES should be u0 and u2 (u1, an unanswered key, is the only non-accepting state). (2) The transition (u0, !has_door_key & door_open) -> u2 is unreachable: the door opens only by consuming a key, which the machine must first observe via u0->u1, so the answer transition always fires from u1. As written it pays 1.0 for an event that cannot occur; drop it for compactness. Fix the final-state set (and ideally remove the dead u0->u2 edge) and resubmit.

REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u0, u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key & !door_open) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, !has_door_key & door_open) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, !door_open & has_door_key) -> u1
(u2, !door_open & !has_door_key) -> u0
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key & !door_open, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, !has_door_key & door_open, u2) -> 1.0
(u2, !door_open & has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
feedback: Accepted. The three-state cycle (u0 idle → u1 key held → u2 answered) faithfully models the recurring obligation 'open the door whenever you carry the key'. Coverage: every state has explicit conditions plus an else self-loop, so proposition-irrelevant steps (turning, moving, waiting, toggling with no effect) are total self-loops; within u1 the valuation is frozen until the answer event, within u2 until the relock, matching the environment's dynamics. Predicates: only has_door_key and door_open are used, no invented events; the answer is correctly detected as the simultaneous change !has_door_key & door_open, which the environment guarantees can only result from the agent's keyed toggle, so the 1.0 reward is always agent-caused. FINAL_STATES is present, nonempty, and semantically right for this recurring task: u1 is the sole rejecting state (an unanswered key at truncation), while u0 (no pending key, including the vacuous zero-gift episode) and u2 (last gift answered, door still open) are accepting — exactly mirroring the environment's success flag. Regression/reset transitions are explicit and both reachable: u2 → u0 when the door shuts with no new key, and u2 → u1 when a key lands at the shutting step (a documented possibility), so consecutive gift cycles are all supported. Rewards are dense but bounded: 0.1 on entering the obligation state (identical formula on both incoming edges) plus 1.0 per answered gift, at most ~13 cycles → ≤ ~14.3 total; no farming is possible because key arrivals are exogenous and capped, and ignoring a gift strands the RM in u1 with no further reward, so the shaping preserves the optimal policy (answer each gift promptly). Format complies with the paper layout (STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION); all states are declared, every reward entry matches a declared transition with an identical formula, and unlisted transitions default to 0. The seed-1 example trace replays correctly: 8 cycles of 0.1+1.0, ending in u0.

Both functions are persistent conditions describing current state after the step, consistent with their 'condition' kind; neither references nor mutates `env.episode_memory` or `previous_valuation`, which is appropriate since event comparison is not required here. There are no imports, no actions, no side effects, and no mutation of the environment; only documented API members (`env.carrying`, `env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, attributes `type` and `is_open`) are used. Syntax is valid Python and the code is safe to execute. Alignment with the code-notes truth conditions is exact for both predicates.
